findings.quote: A nonliving thing may copy some of them, but not cells and not all the rest.
findings.problem: This general rule says no nonliving thing has cells. It fails at a standard exception: dead organisms and once-living material (a dead leaf, a log, cork) are made of cells but are not alive. Hooke's first 'cells' were dead cork cells. The lesson never teaches dead or once-living things, so a student who uses this shortcut as a test will judge wood or a dry leaf to be living because it has cells.
findings.source: OpenStax Biology 2e, 4.1 Studying Cells (Hooke observed cells in cork, dead plant tissue); content-checklist B01; reader-rules.md, Added after the Sol audit

findings.quote: All tilapia in one lake are one species in one area, so that is a population.
findings.problem: Tilapia is not one species. It is the common name for nearly a hundred species of cichlid fish, and the Philippines has both Mozambique tilapia (introduced 1950) and Nile tilapia (introduced 1972). The worked step states a false fact as the reason the group is a population, and the same premise sits in the example's question and the illustration marker. A student who knows that several tilapia species share a lake gets a contradictory reason for the key.
findings.source: Wikipedia, Tilapia (opening sentence and Philippine introductions), accessed 2026-11-03; content-checklist B01, B02

findings.quote: To infer means to reach a conclusion from the evidence you have plus facts you already know.
findings.problem: This paragraph has five sentences; paragraphs must be one to three short sentences. The Cellular organization and Reproduction paragraphs each have four. Round-1 finding L22a is partly fixed but still open in these paragraphs.
